task1.title: Location and types of dance classes attended by young people in an Australian town
task1.prompt: The charts below give information on the location and types of dance classes young people in a town in Australia are currently attending.

visuals.caption: Types of dance classes (by age group)

chartDesc.overview: Private studios are by far the most common location for dance classes, catering to almost half of all students. In terms of class types, younger children (under 11) predominantly attend Ballet, while older students (11–16) prefer Modern dance.
keyFeatures: Pie Chart: Private studios account for nearly half of all dance class locations at 48%, while College-based studios represent the smallest proportion at 10%.
Pie Chart: School halls (after-school) and Community halls & other make up 24% and 18% of class locations respectively.
Bar Chart: For students under 11, Ballet is the most popular type with 600 students, whereas Modern dance is the least popular with 300 students.
Bar Chart: For students aged 11–16, Modern dance attracts the highest number of attendees at approximately 520 students, while Ballet drops to 300 students.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

task2.title: Buying food produced all over the world
task2.prompt:
In many countries nowadays, consumers can go to a supermarket and buy food produced all over the world.

Do you think this is a positive or negative development?
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
